title: OpenVTON-Bench: A Large-Scale High-Resolution Benchmark for Controllable Virtual Try-On Evaluation
claim: Quality should be judged along several interpretable dimensions, combining semantic judgment by a VLM with a structure-aware representation metric.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; hexagon hub-and-spoke left, two stacked pipelines right
description: The left panel, titled 'Proposed 5-Dimensional Evaluation Framework', is a hub-and-spoke layout. Five color-coded hexagons surround a central gallery image with a human figure. They are Background Consistency (blue), Person Consistency (green), Texture Fidelity (yellow), Shape Preservation (orange) and Overall Realism (red). Each has an icon and short example keywords, and arrows point inward to the hub. An arrow leads from the hub to a 'Holistic & Human-Aligned VTON Assessment' box. The right panel, 'Objective Evaluation Methods', has two stacked sections. The top green section, VLM-based Semantic Scoring, takes garment, ground-truth and generated images into a VLM with yes/no questions, which produces a score vector. The bottom yellow section, Representation-based Hierarchical Metric, runs a representation model and a segmentation model with multi-scale erosion, giving global identity consistency and multi-scale garment fidelity scores.
caption: The Proposed Hybrid Evaluation Framework. We move beyond single-scalar metrics by decomposing VTON quality into five human-aligned dimensions. Uniquely, our framework combines (Top) a VLM-as-a-Judge module for semantic auditing with (Bottom) a Multi-Scale Representation Metric that verifies structure-aware garment consistency. This synergy ensures both semantic plausibility and accurate garment replication.
abstract: Recent advances in diffusion models have significantly elevated the visual fidelity of Virtual Try-On (VTON) systems, yet reliable evaluation remains a persistent bottleneck. Traditional metrics struggle to quantify fine-grained texture details and semantic consistency, while existing datasets fail to meet commercial standards in scale and diversity. We present OpenVTON-Bench, a large-scale benchmark comprising approximately 100K high-resolution image pairs (up to $1536\times1536$). The dataset combines Gemini-powered dense captioning with stratified sampling across 20 visual clusters obtained by DINOv3 K-Means. To support reliable evaluation, we propose a multi-modal protocol that measures VTON quality along five interpretable dimensions: background consistency, identity fidelity, texture fidelity, shape plausibility, and overall realism. The protocol integrates VLM-based semantic reasoning with a novel Multi-Scale Representation Metric based on SAM3 segmentation and morphological erosion, enabling the separation of boundary alignment errors from internal texture artifacts. Under the specified evaluation rubric, our representation metric shows strong agreement with human model rankings (Kendall's $Ï$ of 0.833 vs. 0.611 for SSIM). Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/RenxingIntelligence/OpenVTON-Bench.
